Trace, implement and test: leetcode373 find k pairs with smallest sums priority queue using tuple

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
#include <algorithm>
#include <vector>
#include <queue>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    vector<vector<int>> kSmallestPairs(vector<int>& nums1, vector<int>& nums2, int k) {
        vector<vector<int>> res;
        int n = nums1.size(), m = nums2.size();
        if (n == 0 || m == 0)
            return res;

        priority_queue<tuple<int, int, int>, vector<tuple<int, int, int>>, greater<>> pq;
        pq.push({nums1[0] + nums2[0], 0, 0});
        while (pq.size() && res.size() < k)
        {
            auto topP = pq.top();
            int i = get<1>(topP);
            int j = get<2>(topP);
            pq.pop();

            res.push_back({nums1[i], nums2[j]});
            if (j == 0 && i + 1 < n)
                pq.push({nums1[i + 1] + nums2[j], i + 1, j}); /* 关键操作 */

            if (i < n && j + 1 < m)
                pq.push({nums1[i] + nums2[j + 1], i, j + 1});
        }
        return res;
    }
};

// Test
int main()
{
    Solution sol;
    int n = 12;
    vector<int> nums1 = {1, 7, 11}, nums2 = {2, 4, 6};
    int k = 3;
    auto res = sol.kSmallestPairs(nums1, nums2, k);
        
    return 0;
}
